data.current_description: Entry point to the x402 Carbon Retirement API on Base. Returns every endpoint you need plus a live snapshot of the top 3 carbon classes and marketplace listings by liquidity. Discover, quote and certificate are free. Retiring is paid: each retirement costs the credit price plus a fee, sent from your own wallet (prepare/retire) or relayed from a signed USDC authorization (prepare-auth + POST actions/retire). Full spec at /openapi.json. Paid per call with a standard x402 v2 `exact` USDC payment on Base, settled by the Coinbase facilitator. GET /api/discover returns the full catalog for free.

Responses include USDC-per-tonne prices and project metadata for each listing.

data.current_summary: Build the authorization to sign for a relayed retirement
data.current_description: Use to pay for a retirement without sending a transaction. Returns EIP-712 `typedData` (EIP-3009 for USDC, EIP-2612 permit for kVCM) and a ready-to-send `actionsRetireRequest`. Sign `typedData` exactly as returned, set `authPayload.signature`, and POST the request to /api/actions/retire. Requires `details.beneficiaryAddress` or `beneficiaryIsPayer=true`. Paid: the signed authorization funds the retirement, costing the credit price plus a fee and executor gas.
data.summary_suggestion: Generate EIP-712 authorization for relayed retirement
data.description_suggestion: Use to retire carbon credits without submitting a transaction yourself. Returns EIP-712 `typedData` for signing (EIP-3009 for USDC or EIP-2612 for kVCM) and a ready-to-send `actionsRetireRequest`. Sign the `typedData` exactly as returned, add the signature to `authPayload.signature`, and POST the complete request to /api/actions/retire. Requires either `details.beneficiaryAddress` or `beneficiaryIsPayer=true`. Cost is the credit price plus service fee plus executor gas, all covered by the signed authorization.

data.current_summary: Retire carbon credits, paid with a signed x402 authorization
data.current_description: Use to retire carbon credits and receive the Carbonmark certificate in one call. Non-custodial: the payer's signed USDC (EIP-3009) or kVCM (EIP-2612) authorization funds the settlement contract directly, and the service only relays it. POST without `authPayload` to receive the 402 challenge; POST again with the signature in `authPayload`, posting `actionsRetireRequest` verbatim (including `salt`). Cost is the retirement price + fee + executor gas, all inside the signed budget; any unspent budget is refunded in the same transaction.
data.description_suggestion: Executes a retirement transaction using a signed authorization from /api/prepare-auth. Non-custodial: the payer's signed USDC (EIP-3009) or kVCM (EIP-2612) authorization funds the settlement directly; the service only relays it. First POST without `authPayload` to receive the x402 payment challenge. Then POST again with the signature in `authPayload`, sending the `actionsRetireRequest` verbatim (including `salt`). Returns the Carbonmark certificate URL upon success. Total cost (credit price + fee + executor gas) is deducted from the signed authorization; any unspent amount is refunded in the same transaction.
data.reasoning: Summary is clear and domain-appropriate. Description is complex but lacks clarity on the two-step flow and doesn't explain what the 402 challenge is. Missing information about what the operation returns (certificate URL). Enhanced description to clarify the two-step POST pattern, explain the x402 challenge, specify the return value, and make the non-custodial flow more understandable for AI agents deciding between this and prepareRetire.
